quests.instruction: Which word is the opposite of “bright”? (a sunny classroom at noon vs. a closet with the door pulled shut)
quests.hint: What would you reach for if the power went out in a room with no windows?
quests.explanation: Bright means filled with plenty of light. Dark means there’s hardly any light, so it’s hard to see.
quests.funFact: Light travels so fast that a beam could circle the Earth about seven times in one second.

quests.instruction: Aarav’s room was neat on Saturday morning. By evening, clothes and toys were scattered everywhere, so it looked…
quests.hint: Picture hunting for a single sock in a room like that.
quests.explanation: Tidy means everything is in its place. When things are scattered around, we call it messy.
quests.funFact: The word “tidy” comes from an old English word meaning “in good time”.

quests.instruction: Maya finished the puzzle with ten big pieces in a minute. The puzzle with five hundred tiny pieces was…
quests.hint: Which puzzle would keep you busy all weekend?
quests.explanation: Easy tasks can be done without much effort. Difficult ones take lots of time and careful thinking.
quests.funFact: Jigsaw puzzles were first made around 1760, when a mapmaker cut a map into pieces to teach geography.

quests.instruction: The highway has six lanes side by side. The footpath between two old houses fits just one person. It’s very…
quests.hint: Which space could you only walk through single file?
quests.explanation: Wide means there’s lots of space from one side to the other. Narrow means that distance is small.
quests.funFact: Some alleys in Venice, Italy, are so narrow that you can touch both walls at once.

quests.instruction: At the pool, little children splash in the shallow end. Swimmers who want to dive head to the ___ end.
quests.hint: Picture standing on tiptoe in water that is over your head.
quests.explanation: Shallow water doesn’t go far down. Deep water has a long way between the surface and the bottom.
quests.funFact: The deepest known spot in the ocean, the Mariana Trench, is almost eleven kilometres down.

quests.instruction: Which word is the opposite of “boy”?
quests.hint: Think of the two words your class register uses to sort the children.
quests.explanation: Boy and girl are the two words we use for young males and young females.
quests.funFact: Both “boy” and “girl” have been used in English for more than six hundred years.

quests.instruction: A polished marble floor feels smooth. The bark on an old oak tree feels…
quests.hint: Run your fingertips over a window, then over a piece of sandpaper.
quests.explanation: Smooth surfaces have no bumps, so your hand glides across. Rough ones are bumpy or scratchy.
quests.funFact: Sandpaper is made by gluing tiny grains of grit to paper so it can scrape wood smooth.

quests.instruction: Which word is the opposite of “straight”? (the edge of a ruler vs. a banana)
quests.hint: A banana on the table has an outline that isn’t ruler-straight.
quests.explanation: A straight line goes in one direction without bending. A curved line bends gently, like a smile or a banana.
quests.funFact: A rainbow is really a full circle, but from the ground we usually see only the top arc.

quests.instruction: Anna’s kitchen scissors snip paper in a flash. Her toy scissors from nursery won’t even cut a leaf. They’re…
quests.hint: Why do safety scissors for very young children have rounded tips?
quests.explanation: A sharp edge is thin enough to slice through things. A blunt one is thick or rounded, so it just pushes against what it touches.
quests.funFact: Sharp edges cut because all the pushing force is squeezed into a very thin line.

quests.instruction: Mom asks, “Would you like more broccoli?” If you’ve had plenty, you politely say…
quests.hint: Which short word turns down a second helping?
quests.explanation: Yes agrees or accepts. No refuses or disagrees.
quests.funFact: In Japanese, “hai” means yes and “iie” means no.

quests.instruction: “Fish live in water” is a true sentence. “Fish ride bicycles to school” is…
quests.hint: You can test the sentence by looking into a pond: do you see fish riding bikes?
quests.explanation: A true statement matches what really happens. A false one doesn’t match, however fun it sounds.
quests.funFact: On a true-or-false quiz, you have a fifty-fifty chance of getting the answer right just by guessing.

quests.instruction: Which word is the opposite of “summer”? (ice-cream days and swimming vs. woolly scarves and snow)
quests.hint: Which season has the longest, coldest nights where snow falls?
quests.explanation: Summer is the hottest season of the year, while winter is the coldest. They sit on opposite sides of the year’s weather.
quests.funFact: Earth is tilted, so when it’s summer in the north, it’s winter in the south.

quests.instruction: Which word is the opposite of “ask”? (a student wondering who painted the picture vs. a student telling who painted it)
quests.hint: In a chat, one person starts with a question. What does the other person do?
quests.explanation: To ask is to seek information. To answer is to give it back.
quests.funFact: Spanish begins questions with an upside-down question mark: ¿

quests.instruction: You buy a toy at a shop. The shopkeeper’s job is to ___ it.
quests.hint: Picture two people at a shop counter: one hands over the toy, one hands over the money.
quests.explanation: Buying and selling happen together: one person gives money, the other gives goods.
quests.funFact: Before money, people swapped goods directly. That’s called bartering.

quests.instruction: Which word is the opposite of “win”? (a team holding up the trophy vs. a team shaking hands and walking off)
quests.hint: Think about which team goes home without the cup.
quests.explanation: To win is to finish ahead. To lose is to finish behind.
quests.funFact: When a match ends with equal scores, it’s called a tie or a draw.

quests.instruction: A wooden raft floats on the lake. A heavy stone dropped into the lake will…
quests.hint: Where does a pebble end up when you toss it in a pond?
quests.explanation: Floating means staying on top of the water. Sinking means going down below it.
quests.funFact: Huge steel ships float because their shape holds lots of air and pushes lots of water aside.

quests.instruction: The whole row giggled during the funny part of the movie. At the sad ending, little Tom began to…
quests.hint: One of these reactions comes with tears instead of giggles.
quests.explanation: To laugh is to make happy sounds. To cry is to let tears fall, often when you feel upset.
quests.funFact: Babies usually laugh for the very first time when they’re around three or four months old.

quests.instruction: Nina jumped off the high diving board without a worry. Her brother stood at the edge, trembling. Nina was brave, so he was…
quests.hint: How do your knees feel when you look down from somewhere very high?
quests.explanation: Brave means ready to face something that frightens you. Scared means the fear is winning.
quests.funFact: Goosebumps can appear when you’re cold or frightened, a leftover from when our ancestors had much thicker body hair.

quests.instruction: Ollie shared his crayons with a new classmate. That was kind. Grabbing the crayons and laughing would be…
quests.hint: How would the new classmate feel on their first day?
quests.explanation: Kind actions make people feel good and welcome. Mean actions hurt people’s feelings.
quests.funFact: The word “kind” is related to “kin”, an old word for family.

quests.instruction: A weightlifter raises the heavy bar over his head because he’s strong. A newborn bird that can’t stand up yet is…
quests.hint: A newborn bird needs its parents for almost everything, even standing.
quests.explanation: Strong means having lots of power. Weak means having very little.
quests.funFact: Ants can carry loads many times heavier than their own bodies.

quests.instruction: Grandfather has had many, many birthdays. His grandson has had only five. Grandfather is old, and the boy is…
quests.hint: We use “new” for things. Which word do we use for people with few birthdays?
quests.explanation: Old and young describe how many years someone has lived. Things we just bought are new, but people with few years are young.
quests.funFact: Some giant tortoises live for well over a hundred years.

quests.instruction: It’s pouring, so the kids play indoors. When the rain stops, they run…
quests.hint: Where do you go to jump in puddles?
quests.explanation: Inside means within walls and a roof. Outside is the open space beyond them.
quests.funFact: Inside an igloo, body heat can keep the air many degrees warmer than the freezing air outside.

quests.instruction: A helmet helps keep you safe on a bike. Racing down a steep hill with no brakes is…
quests.hint: Imagine the choice that could end with a plaster, or worse.
quests.explanation: Safe means unlikely to hurt anyone. Dangerous means there’s a real chance of getting hurt.
quests.funFact: Wearing a bike helmet lowers the chance of a serious head injury.

quests.instruction: After running three laps, Dev felt tired. Sam had just woken from a long nap and felt…
quests.hint: Who’s ready to race again right now?
quests.explanation: Tired means your body needs rest. Energetic means you feel full of get-up-and-go.
quests.funFact: Children need more hours of sleep than adults so their bodies can grow.

quests.instruction: The last minutes of the tied match had everyone on their feet. Watching a slow video of paint drying would feel…
quests.hint: Which would make you check the clock again and again?
quests.explanation: Exciting things grab your attention and make your heart race. Boring things don’t hold your interest.
quests.funFact: “Exciting” comes from a Latin word meaning “to rouse” or “to wake up”.

quests.instruction: Everyone giggled at the clown’s wobbly dance. At the assembly about road safety, the principal used a ___ voice.
quests.hint: Listen to how a doctor speaks when giving important instructions.
quests.explanation: Funny moments make us laugh. A serious moment calls for careful, calm attention instead.
quests.funFact: Theatre is often shown as two masks: one smiling and one frowning.

quests.instruction: Fans shout to cheer on their team. In the library, you need to…
quests.hint: What do you do when a sleeping baby is nearby?
quests.explanation: To shout is to speak very loudly. To whisper is to speak very softly so only a person close by hears.
quests.funFact: A whisper doesn’t use your vocal cords, which is why it sounds airy.

quests.instruction: Which word is the opposite of “smile”? (a face with corners turned up vs. a face with eyebrows pulled together and corners turned down)
quests.hint: Which expression would you make while trying to solve a really tough puzzle?
quests.explanation: A smile lifts the corners of your mouth to show you’re pleased. A frown pulls the face down to show you’re unhappy or thinking hard.
quests.funFact: The first smiley :-) typed with keyboard characters was sent in 1982 by Scott Fahlman.

quests.instruction: The teacher asked, “Who forgot their homework?” Every hand stayed down, so ___ of the students had forgotten it.
quests.hint: How many hands went up?
quests.explanation: All means every single one. None means not even one.
quests.funFact: The number zero is how we write “none”.

quests.instruction: Zoe’s sum got a tick from the teacher, so her answer was right. Max’s got a cross, so his answer was…
quests.hint: What does the teacher’s cross tell you?
quests.explanation: Right means correct, exactly as it should be. Wrong means incorrect, with a mistake in it.
quests.funFact: The word “right” can mean correct, the opposite of left, or something you’re allowed to do.
